args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy with an error rate of 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 was promoted to production. Follow-up needed: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and review why the release was promoted despite the unhealthy staging RC.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Before:** v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions.
- **After:** the service reports healthy with a 0.2% error rate. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery. There were no other open incidents, so it isn't a duplicate.

Also worth looking at: the test version of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was already unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. I listed two follow-ups in the incident: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and why it went to production after failing in staging.
